clue.text: Only one kind of bone in a catheter ruined several tubes

indicators.note: a T-bone is a kind of bone, so keeping only one of that kind means one of the two T letters must go
something ruined is wrecked out of its old shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical scene: a damaged catheter with a bone lodged in it has wrecked several tubes.
explanation.walkthrough: A T-bone is a cut of steak; 'only one' T-bone means A CATHETER keeps just one of its two Ts before the remaining letters are reshuffled into TRACHEAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracheae is the plural of trachea, the windpipe, so the word names several breathing tubes.

clue.text: Leader's vehicle negotiating chicane

indicators.note: a car negotiating a bend goes around it, so the vehicle wraps around the bend's letter

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
a chicane is a tight double bend, shaped like the letter Z

explanation.surface: A racing driver steers a car through a chicane on the track.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': Leader is the wordplay that follows. A chicane is a Z-shaped kink on a racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: A czar was the emperor of Russia, and the title is now used for any powerful appointed chief or supremo.

clue.text: Military wear that's keeping fashionable

indicators.note: one word keeping another holds it inside itself

blocks.note: the word that, with 's as the verb joining it to the rest
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A note on army uniform that manages to stay stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is part of the container word, not a verb to be skipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin hat is informal for a soldier's steel helmet, a piece of military headgear.

clue.text: Seat stretched round you, say

indicators.note: say tells us to take the word by its sound, a single letter pronounced the same
one word placed round another encloses it

blocks.note: something stretched has been made longer
the letter U is pronounced like you

explanation.surface: A chair that has been extended around the person sitting in it.
explanation.walkthrough: LONGER goes round U: LO-U-NGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounger is a reclining chair, such as a sun lounger by a pool, so it is a kind of seat.

clue.text: A pastoral god goes round loop, endlessly referring to cosmic extremes

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter
the god goes round the shortened word, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written
Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and flocks
a helix is a spiral, a series of loops

explanation.surface: A rustic deity circling round a loop while musing on the far reaches of space.
explanation.walkthrough: A helix is a spiral, a run of loops; 'endlessly' trims it before the god wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphelian is the adjective from aphelion, the point in an orbit farthest from the sun, one of its cosmic extremes.

clue.text: Victorian boy may have worn such hearty hearts, perhaps

definitions.text: Victorian boy may have worn such

blocks.note: 'my hearties' is how a sailor addresses shipmates, so a hearty is a sailor
hearts is one example of a suit in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A Victorian lad in his best clothes, cheerfully full of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearty' looks like an adjective, but here it is a noun for a seaman; 'perhaps' marks hearts as one example of a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Navy-style outfits with wide collars were standard dress for small boys in Victorian Britain.

clue.text: Boy holds girl hostage

indicators.note: one name that holds another has it gripped inside

blocks.note: Ken is a boy's name
Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A lad takes a girl hostage.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Keenan was held hostage in Beirut from 1986 to 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Keenan, the Irish writer, is famous as a hostage kidnapped and held for over four years in Lebanon.

clue.text: Money for French vintage? O to quaff one!

indicators.note: to quaff is to drink something down, taking it inside

blocks.note: cru is the French term for a wine or vineyard of a given quality
the letter O stands for nought
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone longs to drink a fine French wine and wonders what it costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O' looks like an exclamation, but it is the round figure nought.
explanation.definitionFit: The cruzeiro was the currency of Brazil for much of the twentieth century.

clue.text: A female bird is one that embraces a male

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one word encloses the others

blocks.note: one female bird, as the definition says: a pen is a female swan
taken as written
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A hen bird cuddling up to a male.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' points back to the definition: another female bird, the swan's mate, does the embracing.
explanation.definitionFit: A peahen is the female peafowl, the drab mate of the showy peacock.

clue.text: Having removed loud muffler, revealed ugly mark

indicators.note: having removed something, the word is left without that letter

blocks.note: f is forte, the musical direction for loud
a muffler is a warm scarf

explanation.surface: Someone takes off a noisy car silencer, or a scarf, to show a blemish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muffler' suggests an exhaust silencer, but here it is the old word for a scarf; take F from SCARF.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark left on skin after a wound heals, often seen as unsightly.

clue.text: Deer with broken antler inside area not far from coast

indicators.note: something broken is smashed up, so its letters are rearranged
inside tells us the reworked letters go within the deer

blocks.note: a hind is a female deer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deer with a damaged antler roaming the countryside near the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: The reworked letters sit before the deer's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinterland is the inland region lying behind a coast or port, close to it but away from the shore.

clue.text: Exercises turning fish into something edible

indicators.note: turning round makes the word read the other way

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
the tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: Workouts that somehow transform a fish into a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: PE then TUNA backwards, ANUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is an edible seed eaten as a snack, so it is something that can be eaten.

clue.text: Say goodbye in the den on going up, going swimmingly!

indicators.note: in places the farewell inside the following words
in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: a lair is an animal's den
taken as written
ta-ta is an informal way to say goodbye

explanation.surface: Waving farewell from a den as things go well and rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The farewell sits between the O and N of 'on', and only then does the whole string read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Natatorial means relating to swimming, so it describes something that is going by swimming, with a pun on 'swimmingly'.

clue.text: Someone leaving the country upsets me, admittedly

indicators.note: upsets turns a word over, so it reads from the other end

blocks.note: taken as written
'I grant' is said when admitting a point, as in 'I grant you'

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that a departing traveller upsets them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsets' looks like an anagram signal but just flips ME; 'admittedly' becomes the phrase 'I grant'.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant is a person who leaves their own country to settle elsewhere.

clue.text: Ersatz South Africa abandoned, cutting the swine who once ran it

indicators.note: letters abandoned are left behind, so they are taken out
something cutting into another goes inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
a hog is a pig, a swine

explanation.surface: A sham South Africa is deserted, slicing through a pig who once governed it.
explanation.walkthrough: J.B.M. Hertzog was Prime Minister of South Africa from 1924 to 1939; 'it' in the definition is South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: James Hertzog led the South African government as Prime Minister for fifteen years between the wars.

clue.text: Muse upset over reluctant material

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the name upside down so it reads backwards

blocks.note: Clio is the Muse of history
loth means unwilling, reluctant

explanation.surface: A goddess of inspiration is upset with an unwilling subject.
explanation.walkthrough: CLIO upwards is OILC, sitting over LOTH in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilcloth is cotton cloth treated with oil to make it waterproof, used for tablecloths, so a type of material.

clue.text: Gets a notion of time among northern peoples

indicators.note: among puts one thing in the midst of others

blocks.note: the Inuit are peoples of the Arctic north
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An anthropologist gets an idea of how Arctic peoples see time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inuit of the Arctic are taken here with an English plural S.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit is to sense or grasp something by instinct, so intuits means gets a notion without reasoning.

clue.text: Have eye on a drink from the building

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits directly above it

blocks.note: a private eye is a detective, shortened to tec
tonic water is a drink

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a drink being brought from the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have eye on' reads like keeping watch, but the eye is a private detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Tectonic comes from the Greek for builder and means relating to building or construction, as in tectonic arts.

clue.text: A little US money left in focus

blocks.note: a cent is a small unit of American currency
red stands for the political left

explanation.surface: A small sum of American cash is left at the centre of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Red is the colour of left-wing politics.
explanation.definitionFit: When an image is centred in a lens or frame it is properly aimed and in focus.

clue.text: Apertures dismissed as futile

indicators.note: dismissed here means sent off and broken up, so the letters are scattered and reformed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Openings are written off as pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Fistulae are abnormal passages or openings in the body, such as between organs or to the skin.

clue.text: A tide turning: end of pipe dream

indicators.note: turning here churns the letters into a new order
end of means take only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of pipe

explanation.surface: A turning tide at the end of a pipe, like a pipe dream.
explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form ideas or imagine, so it fits dream as a verb meaning conceive in the mind.

clue.text: Coup de chien, as the French say

indicators.note: we must imagine the word spoken in a French accent

blocks.note: de chien is French for of a dog; a dog is a pooch

explanation.surface: A French phrase that looks like a stroke of luck, or a dog's trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Coup de chien is a 'dog's coup', a pooch's coup; said with a French accent pooch comes out close to the German word for an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is a sudden violent attempt to overthrow a government, which is exactly a coup.

clue.text: Clean up on a fruity goddess

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: to mop is to clean a floor
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Clearing up after a fruit-loving deity.
explanation.walkthrough: MOP reversed is POM, then ON and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomona was the Roman goddess of fruit trees and orchards, hence a goddess of fruit.

clue.text: Favourite drink contains, oddly, a lot of jelly

indicators.note: oddly means arranged in a strange way, so these letters are shuffled
the drink contains the reworked letters inside it

blocks.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
rum is a drink
taken as written

explanation.surface: A favourite tipple has, strangely, a great deal of jelly in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like an instruction to take odd letters, but here it means shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrolatum is the technical name for petroleum jelly, the greasy ointment better known as Vaseline.

clue.text: Image by Ike to be beside the  seaside?

blocks.note: surface: a picture of, or by, someone called Ike

blocks.clueFragment: by Ike to be beside the  seaside?
blocks.note: setter's reading: recall the first line of the old music-hall song about the seaside and take the letters that stand just before Ike

explanation.walkthrough: In the song line 'I do like to be beside the seaside', the letters I-DO-L sit right beside IKE, giving a word for an image.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image or statue of a god used as an object of worship.

clue.text: On the pull, women left digging

indicators.note: the letter for women has left, so it is dropped from the word

blocks.note: on and in both mean happening or taking place, as in 'the party is on'
a tow is a pull
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Out on the pull, the women left at a dig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the pull' is British slang for looking for a romantic partner, but here the phrase splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Into and digging are both slang for keen on: if you're into something, you dig it.

clue.text: House expresses disapproval about artist coming back

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other
coming back means the whole thing returns, read from right to left

blocks.note: someone who tuts is making a sound of disapproval
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A household tuts at an artist returning home.
explanation.walkthrough: The artist goes in after the first letter, and then everything reads backwards. RA means Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stuarts were the royal house that ruled Scotland and later England, so house means a dynasty here.

clue.text: In Germany, a stone version of Albert

blocks.note: ein is German for a
Stein is German for stone

explanation.surface: A German stone carving of a man called Albert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Germany' covers both words: the surname literally means 'a stone' in German.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, the German-born physicist, is the most famous bearer of that first name.
